$comment: P5-17 — a deliberately stale curated model list, for the drift path's own test.
README §22.7's 'Done when' clause is 'a deliberately stale model list opens a PR'. That can only
be proved deterministically if the stale state is a fixture rather than something a live provider
has to be coaxed into — a real provider would have to change its catalogue, which is neither
repeatable nor something a test should be able to cause.
So this file describes a provider whose curated fallback list contains a model the discovered
list does not have. `test-provider-contract-gate.ts` drives it through the same runner, report
and GitHub-decision code the nightly job uses, and asserts the whole chain ends in a pull-request
plan. No network, no key, no provider.
The shapes are the ones the runner consumes: a curated descriptor list, what `listModels()`
actually returned, and the browser observation. A 'removed' model is present in the curated list
and absent from the discovered list — which is the case §17.2's chooser turns into a selection that
fails when a user clicks it.

provider.name: Fixture provider with a stale curated list

$rationale: The removed model is the defect: the chooser offers something the provider no longer serves.
The added model rides along in the same diff but is not by itself breakage, so it appears in the
drift issue rather than a breakage one.
test() passing is what keeps this a drift finding and not a breakage finding — the two have to
stay separately triggerable or a provider that both broke and lost a model produces one
ambiguous issue instead of two actionable ones.
